leaves.name: carayolThmA
leaves.doc: Carayol 1986, Theoreme (A), at F = Q, weight 2, packaged printed form over K_{f,lambda} (r17-print, r17-rebase): for a printed newform f (Tau Ceti Newform N 2) with number field K_f and a place lambda | l of K_f, there is a continuous rho : G_Q -> GL_2(K_{f,lambda}) (Mathlib adicCompletion), absolutely irreducible in Burnside's form (the image spans M_2(K_{f,lambda})), unramified at p not dividing N l with arithmetic-Frobenius trace a_p(f), whose Serre-Tate conductor exponent at every prime p != l is v_p(N). The passage to r17 (IsNewform = printed newform; extension of scalars to Qbar_l; absolute irreducibility gives semisimplicity; conductor invariance under scalar extension and isomorphism; Brauer-Nesbitt with Chebotarev) is proved in Lean. Replaces r17.
leaves.flag: unread: new printed leaf (packaged form); reading risk: Carayol 1986 Theoreme (A) as printed is local-global compatibility of rho_{f,lambda}|G_{Q_p} with pi_{f,p} through the local Langlands correspondence; the leaf's conductor clause (condExp = v_p(N) at p != l) follows from it only with Casselman 1973 (a(pi_p) = v_p(N) for newforms) and the conductor compatibility of the local correspondence (locator audit row R17 rates the conductor equality a CONSEQUENCE of these); it is printed as one statement only if the packaged form in Darmon-Diamond-Taylor 1997 Thm 3.1 or Carayol section 0.8 states it (UNVERIFIED); if the statement check finds the packaging unprinted, re-flag 'pending reading' (count-neutral) or fold the split form (CarayolExistence + CarayolConductor). Burnside's form of absolute irreducibility is a step beyond Ribet's printed 'irreducible' (proved in Lean from irreducible + odd in CarayolPrintedIrr); locators UNVERIFIED
leaves.source: Carayol, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 19 (1986) 409-468, Theoreme (A), pp. 409-411 and section 0.8 p. 411 (coverage read by the locator audit, row R17); Casselman, Math. Ann. 201 (1973) (a(pi_p) = v_p(N)); Ribet, LNM 601 (1977) Thm 2.3 (irreducibility); Shimura 1971 Thm 7.14 and Deligne 1971 (existence, traces, det); Darmon-Diamond-Taylor, Fermat's Last Theorem (1997) Thm 3.1 (packaging); locators UNVERIFIED
